report:
**Conclusion:** Your view is too strong. Evidence supports an *association* between higher olive-oil intake and lower stroke risk, and one major randomized dietary trial supports cardiovascular benefit from a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil. But it does **not** establish that simply adding olive oil to any diet, independent of what it replaces and the overall dietary pattern, reliably prevents stroke.

**Evidence for the claim:** A 2014 meta-analysis combining case-control, cohort, and one intervention trial (38,673 participants for stroke) found an inverse association between olive-oil consumption and stroke. Observational results were adjusted for energy intake, but adjustment cannot eliminate confounding: people using more olive oil may also have healthier diets, incomes, activity levels, and healthcare.  
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-nutrition/article/olive-oil-consumption-and-risk-of-chd-andor-stroke-a-metaanalysis-of-casecontrol-cohort-and-intervention-studies/79A90337470271D8A8CE2FDC77BD869E

PREDIMED, in people aged 55–80 at high cardiovascular risk, found fewer *composite* major cardiovascular events (stroke, heart attack, or cardiovascular death) among participants assigned to Mediterranean diets supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil or nuts versus a reduced-fat diet. This is stronger causal evidence—but it tested a whole dietary intervention, education, and supplied foods, not olive oil alone or “more” olive oil in the general population.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29897866/

A later meta-analysis of prospective cohorts reports that the literature has been inconsistent and focuses chiefly on composite cardiovascular disease and mortality rather than stroke specifically.  
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9623257/

**Bottom line:** “Olive oil reduces stroke risk” is a reasonable but qualified summary when it replaces less-healthful fats within a Mediterranean-style diet. “Consume more olive oil and you will reduce stroke risk” overstates causality and certainty.
